title.zh: 卷231 列傳十八 佟养性 李永芳 石廷柱 马光远 李思忠 金玉和
title.en: Volume 231 Biographies 18: Tong Yang Xing, Li Yongfang, Shi Tingzhu, Ma Guangyuan, Li Sizhong, Jin Yuhe
title.raw: 卷231 列傳十八 佟养性 李永芳 石廷柱 马光远 李思忠 金玉和

sentences.zh: 列傳十八

translations.literal: Biographies 18
translations.idiomatic: Biography 18

sentences.zh: 佟養性孫國瑤李永芳石廷柱馬光遠弟光輝李思忠子廕祖廕祖子鈵金玉和子維城王一屏一屏子國光國光子永譽孫得功張士彥士彥子朝璘金礪

translations.literal: Tong Yangxing; his grandson Guoyao; Li Yongfang; Shi Tingzhu; Ma Guangyuan and his younger brother Guanghui; Li Sizhong, his son Yinzu, his grandson Zuyinzi, and Zuyinzi's son Bin; Jin Yuhe and his son Weicheng; Wang Yiping, Yiping's son Guoguang, and Guoguang's son Yongyu; Sun Degong; Zhang Shiyan and Shiyan's son Chaolin; and Jin Li.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yangxing; his grandson Guoyao; Li Yongfang; Shi Tingzhu; Ma Guangyuan and his younger brother Guanghui; Li Sizhong, his son Yinzu, his grandson Zuyinzi, and Zuyinzi's son Bin; Jin Yuhe and his son Weicheng; Wang Yiping, Yiping's son Guoguang, and Guoguang's son Yongyu; Sun Degong; Zhang Shiyan and Shiyan's son Chaolin; and Jin Li.

sentences.zh: 佟養性，遼東人。

translations.literal: Tong Yangxing was a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yangxing was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 先世本滿洲，居佟佳，以地為氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors were originally Manchu, dwelling at Tongjia, and took the place as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were Manchu who lived at Tongjia and took that place name as their clan.

sentences.zh: 有達爾哈齊者，入明邊為商，自開原徙撫順，遂家焉。

translations.literal: There was one Darhachi who entered the Ming border as a merchant, moved from Kaiyuan to Fushun, and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: A forebear named Darhachi crossed into Ming territory as a trader, relocated from Kaiyuan to Fushun, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 天命建元，太祖日益盛強。

translations.literal: When the Tianming reign era was established, the Taizu grew daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianming era was proclaimed, Taizu grew steadily more powerful.

sentences.zh: 養性潛輸款，為明邊吏所察，置之獄，脫出，歸太祖。

translations.literal: Yangxing secretly offered his allegiance; Ming border officials discovered it, imprisoned him, but he escaped and returned to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing secretly pledged himself to Taizu; Ming border officials detected this, jailed him, but he broke free and went over to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖妻以宗女，號「施吾理額駙」，授三等副將。

translations.literal: The Taizu gave him an imperial clanswoman in marriage, titled him "Shiwuli Efu," and appointed him a third-rank deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu married him to a clanswoman, styled him "Shiwuli Efu," and made him a third-rank deputy general.

sentences.zh: 從克遼東，進二等總兵官。

translations.literal: Following the capture of eastern Liaoning, he was promoted to second-rank commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of eastern Liaodong he was promoted to second-rank commander.

sentences.zh: 太祖用兵於明，明邊吏民歸者，籍丁壯為兵。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned against Ming, Ming border officials and commoners who submitted were registered, and able-bodied men were made soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizu fought Ming, Han officials and people who came over were enrolled and their able men pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 至太宗天聰間，始別置一軍，國語號「烏真超哈」。

translations.literal: Only in the Taizong's Tiancong period was a separate army established, called in the national language "Ujencooha."
translations.idiomatic: Not until Taizong's Tiancong reign was a distinct corps formed, known in Manchu as "Ujencooha."

sentences.zh: 五年正月，命養性為昂邦章京，諭曰：「漢人軍民諸政，付爾總理，各官受節制。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he appointed Yangxing Angbang Zhangjing and instructed him: "All civil and military affairs of the Han people are entrusted to your overall administration; each official is under your command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Yangxing was named Angbang Zhangjing and told: "All Han civil and military affairs are placed in your charge; every officer answers to you.

sentences.zh: 爾其殫厥忠，簡善黜惡，卹兵撫民，毋徇親故，毋蔑疏遠。

translations.literal: You must exhaust your loyalty, promote the good and dismiss the wicked, comfort the troops and soothe the people, do not favor relatives, and do not slight the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Serve with your whole loyalty; elevate the worthy and remove the corrupt; care for soldiers and reassure the people; show no favor to kin, and do not scorn those far from you.

sentences.zh: 昔廉頗、藺相如共為將相，以爭班秩，幾至嫌釁。

translations.literal: In former times Lian Po and Lin Xiangru both served as general and minister; because they disputed precedence they nearly came to mutual resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Lian Po and Lin Xiangru held high civil and military office yet quarreled over rank until they nearly came to open rancor.

sentences.zh: 賴相如舍私奉國，能使令名焜耀於今日。

translations.literal: Thanks to Xiangru setting aside private feeling to serve the state, their good names still shine brightly today.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiangru set private grievance aside for the realm, their good names still shine today.

sentences.zh: 爾尚克效之！」

translations.literal: You too must be able to emulate them!"
translations.idiomatic: You must be able to do likewise!"

sentences.zh: 又諭諸漢官曰：「漢人軍民諸政，命額駙佟養性總理，各官受節制。

translations.literal: He also instructed the Han officials: "All civil and military affairs of the Han people are placed under the overall administration of Efu Tong Yangxing; each official is under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He also told the Han officers: "Han civil and military affairs are entrusted to Efu Tong Yangxing; you are all under his authority.

sentences.zh: 其有勢豪嫉妒不從命者，非特藐養性，是輕國體、褻法令也，必譴毋赦！

translations.literal: If there are powerful bullies who, jealous, refuse to obey, they do not merely despise Yangxing—they slight the dignity of the state and profane the laws; they must be punished without pardon!
translations.idiomatic: Any powerful man who, out of jealousy, refuses to obey does not merely slight Yangxing—he insults the state and defies its laws, and shall be punished without mercy!

sentences.zh: 如能謹守約束，先公後私，壹意為國，則爾曹令名亦永垂後世矣。」

translations.literal: If you can strictly keep discipline, put the public before the private, and devote yourselves wholly to the state, then you too will leave your good names forever to posterity."
translations.idiomatic: If you keep discipline, put the public good first, and serve the realm with undivided purpose, your own good names will endure for generations."

sentences.zh: 是歲，初鑄砲，使養性為監。

translations.literal: That year cannon were first cast, and Yangxing was made superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: That year the first cannon were cast, with Yangxing placed in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 砲成，銘其上曰「天祐助威大將軍」，凡四十具。

translations.literal: When the cannon were finished, they were inscribed "General Tianyou Zhuwei," forty pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: When they were ready, each was inscribed "General Tianyou Zhuwei"; forty pieces were made in all.

sentences.zh: 師行則車載以從，養性掌焉。

translations.literal: When the army marched, they were carried on wagons; Yangxing was in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign they were hauled on wagons under Yangxing's command.

sentences.zh: 八月，上伐明，圍大凌河城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the sovereign attacked Ming and besieged Dalinghe city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the sovereign marched against Ming and laid siege to Dalinghe.

sentences.zh: 養性率所部載砲越走錦州道為營，擊城西台，台兵降；

translations.literal: Yangxing led his unit, hauling cannon along the Jinzhou road to encamp, and bombarded the western platform; the platform troops surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing led his men with the guns along the Jinzhou road, set camp, and shelled the western bastion until its garrison surrendered;

sentences.zh: 又擊城南，壞睥睨；

translations.literal: he again attacked the south of the city and destroyed the parapet;
translations.idiomatic: then battered the south wall and smashed the parapet;

sentences.zh: 翌日，擊城東台，台圮，台兵夜遁，盡殲之。

translations.literal: the next day he attacked the eastern platform; the platform collapsed, the troops fled by night, and all were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: the next day he struck the eastern bastion, which collapsed; the garrison fled by night and was wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 九月，明兵出關援錦州，上遣親軍迎擊，養性以所部兵五百從，敵潰遁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Ming troops came from beyond the pass to relieve Jinzhou; the sovereign sent his personal guard to meet them, and Yangxing followed with five hundred men of his unit; the enemy broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Ming forces came through the pass to relieve Jinzhou; the sovereign sent his household troops to intercept them, and Yangxing followed with five hundred of his own men; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 明監軍道張春合諸路兵援大凌河，夜戰，上督騎兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, Ming supervising army intendant, combined troops from various routes to relieve Dalinghe; they fought at night, and the sovereign led cavalry to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, the Ming army supervisor, united columns to relieve Dalinghe; in a night battle the sovereign led cavalry and routed them.

sentences.zh: 方追奔，明潰兵复陣，上命養性屯敵壘東，發砲毀敵壘。

translations.literal: As they were pursuing the fugitives, Ming broken troops re-formed; the sovereign ordered Yangxing to station east of the enemy stockade and fire cannon to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: While the pursuit was still on, broken Ming units re-formed; the sovereign ordered Yangxing to take position east of their camp and blast the stockade apart with cannon.

sentences.zh: 十月，攻於子章台，發砲擊台上堞，台兵多死者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they attacked Yuzizhang platform, fired on the parapet, and many platform troops died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they assaulted Yuzizhang bastion, shelled the parapet, and killed many of its defenders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，祖大壽以大凌河降，上命盡籍城中所儲槍砲彈藥付養性。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zu Dashou surrendered Dalinghe with the great city; the sovereign ordered all firearms, cannon, and ammunition stored in the city registered and delivered to Yangxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zu Dashou surrendered Dalinghe; the sovereign had every gun, cannon, and round in the city inventoried and handed over to Yangxing.

sentences.zh: 尋率兵隳明所置台壕，自大凌河至於廣寧。

translations.literal: Soon after he led troops to demolish platforms and trenches Ming had built, from Dalinghe to Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops to tear down Ming bastions and trenches from Dalinghe all the way to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，上幸城北演武場閱兵，養性率所部烏真超哈試砲，擐甲列陣，軍容甚肅。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year the sovereign visited the drill ground north of the city to review troops; Yangxing led his Ujencooha to test the cannon, donned armor and drew up formation—the army's bearing was very disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year the sovereign reviewed troops at the drill ground north of the city; Yangxing led his Ujencooha in a gunnery trial, armor on and ranks drawn up, with a discipline that greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 上嘉養性能治軍，因追獎大凌河戰功，賜雕鞍良馬一、白金百，遂遍及諸將，自石廷柱以下皆有賜，設宴以勞之。

translations.literal: The sovereign praised Yangxing's ability to manage troops, and in recognition of his merit at Dalinghe awarded him one carved saddle and a fine horse and a hundred taels of white silver; then he extended rewards to all generals—from Shi Tingzhu downward all received gifts, and a feast was held to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with Yangxing's command of troops, the sovereign rewarded his service at Dalinghe with a carved saddle, a fine horse, and a hundred taels of silver, then extended gifts to every general from Shi Tingzhu down and held a feast in their honor.

sentences.zh: 養性疏言：「新編漢兵，馬步僅三千有奇，宜盡籍漢民為兵，有事持火器而戰，無事則為農。

translations.literal: Yangxing memorialized: "The newly organized Han army has barely three thousand odd horse and foot; it is fitting to register all Han people as soldiers—when there is business they fight with firearms, when there is none they farm.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing memorialized: "The newly formed Han force numbers barely three thousand horse and foot; all Han subjects should be enrolled—armed with firearms in war, farming in peace.

sentences.zh: 火器攻城，非砲不克，三眼槍、佛朗機鳥槍特城守器耳，宜增鑄大砲。

translations.literal: In storming cities with firearms, without cannon it cannot be done; the three-eyed gun, Frankish swivel-gun, and musket are merely weapons for defense of cities—it is fitting to cast more large cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Firearms can take a city only with heavy cannon; three-barreled guns, breech-loading swivel pieces, and muskets serve chiefly for defense—we should cast more large guns.

sentences.zh: 兵食未足，宜令民廣開墾，無力者官畀牛若種，穫則以十一償。」

translations.literal: Provisions for the army are insufficient; it is fitting to order the people to open more land for cultivation; for those without means the government should provide oxen or seed, and at harvest they repay one part in ten."
translations.idiomatic: Army rations are still short; the people should be urged to open new fields, and where they lack means the state should supply oxen or seed, to be repaid at one tenth of the harvest."

sentences.zh: 四月，上自將伐察哈爾，命與貝勒阿巴泰、杜度，大臣揚古利、伊爾登留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the sovereign personally led a campaign against the Chahar, and ordered him to garrison together with princes Abatai and Dudu and ministers Yangguli and Ilden.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the sovereign marched in person against the Chahar and left Yangxing to hold the capital with Princes Abatai and Dudu and ministers Yangguli and Ilden.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 順治間，追諡勤惠。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi period he was posthumously given the temple name Qinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzhi he was posthumously titled Qinhui (Diligent and Kind).

sentences.zh: 子普漢，改襲二等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: His son Puhan changed to inherit second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puhan inherited the title as second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 卒，以弟六十襲。

translations.literal: When he died, his younger brother Liushi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Puhan died, his younger brother Liushi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 崇德四年，漢軍旗制定，隸漢軍正藍旗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongde, when the Han Army Banners were established, he was placed in the Plain Blue Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongde, when the Han Army banners were fixed, the family was assigned to the Plain Blue Han banner.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，改二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, changed to second-rank jingqini hapang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 the rank was changed to second-class jingqini hapang.

sentences.zh: 遇恩詔，累進三等伯。

translations.literal: At benevolent amnesties he was repeatedly advanced to third-rank count.
translations.idiomatic: At successive amnesties the rank rose until he became a third-class count.

sentences.zh: 國瑤，六十子也，襲爵。

translations.literal: Guoyao was Liushi's son and inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyao, Liushi's son, inherited the peerage.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，授本旗副都統。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 he was made deputy lieutenant-general of his banner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反，特命國瑤為鄖陽提督，帥師鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Wu Sangui rebelled, Guoyao was specially appointed Xunyang Brigade Commander to command troops in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12, when Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, Guoyao was specially named brigade commander at Xunyang to hold the region with his troops.

sentences.zh: 十三年，襄陽總兵楊來嘉以穀城叛附三桂，鄖陽副將洪福應來嘉，劫部兵千餘攻國瑤。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Yang Jiajia, brigade commander at Xiangyang, rebelled at Gucheng and joined San Gui; Xunyang deputy commander Hong Fu joined Jiajia, seized over a thousand soldiers of the department, and attacked Guoyao.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Yang Jiajia, the Xiangyang commander, rebelled at Gucheng and went over to Wu Sangui; Hong Fu, deputy at Xunyang, followed him, seized more than a thousand government troops, and attacked Guoyao.

sentences.zh: 國瑤率游擊杜英、佟大年以健丁三百拒戰，福退，復至，苦戰數日，斬二百餘級，福敗遁。

translations.literal: Guoyao led guerrilla commanders Du Ying and Tong Danian with three hundred picked men to resist; Fu retreated, then returned, and after bitter fighting for several days two hundred odd were beheaded and Fu was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyao met them with guerrilla officers Du Ying and Tong Danian and three hundred picked men; Hong Fu withdrew, returned, and after days of hard fighting lost more than two hundred killed before he was driven off.

sentences.zh: 事聞，加左都督。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, he was promoted to Left Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was promoted to Left Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，福挾諸叛將分五道來犯，复擊敗之，逐戰泥河口、板橋河，斬其將林躍等七輩、兵數百人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Fu, with various rebel generals, came to attack in five columns; Guoyao defeated them again, pursued to Nihekou and Banqiaohe, beheaded their generals Lin Yue and seven others and several hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Hong Fu and other rebel commanders advanced in five columns; Guoyao beat them again, pursued them to Nihekou and Banqiaohe, and killed seven of their officers including Lin Yue and several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 十五年，四川叛將譚弘與福等復分道來犯，弘屯鄖江北，福掠鄖江南，相聲援；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Sichuan rebel general Tan Hong with Fu and others again came in separate columns; Hong camped north of the Han River at Xunyang, Fu raided south of the river, coordinating by mutual support;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Sichuan rebel Tan Hong and Hong Fu again attacked by separate routes; Tan Hong held the north bank of the Han at Xunyang while Hong Fu raided the south, each supporting the other;

sentences.zh: 國瑤分兵御之，戰坪溝、戰黃畈、戰九里岡，又渡鄖江戰江南岸，皆勝，焚其舟及械，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: Guoyao divided his forces to resist, fought at Pinggou, Huangfan, and Jiuligang, and again crossed the Han to fight on the south bank—all victories, burning their boats and equipment, beheadings and captures beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyao divided his forces to meet them, fought at Pinggou, Huangfan, and Jiuligang, crossed the Han to strike the south bank, and won every engagement, burning their boats and arms and taking heads and prisoners beyond count.

sentences.zh: 福復遣眾伏鄖江兩岸，以三十餘舟順江下，泊琵琶灘，偪鄖陽運道為寨。

translations.literal: Fu again sent troops to lie in wait on both banks of the Han; more than thirty boats went downriver, moored at Pipa Beach, and built a stockade pressing on the Xunyang supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Fu again posted men on both banks of the Han and sent more than thirty boats downstream to Pipa Beach, where they built a camp threatening the Xunyang supply line.

sentences.zh: 國瑤及將軍噶爾漢、撫治楊茂勳等率水陸兵大破之，戰陡嶺，福敗走，運道复通。

translations.literal: Guoyao with General Garhan, pacification commissioner Yang Maoxun, and others led land and river forces to smash them; at Douling they fought, Fu was defeated and fled, and the supply route was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Guoyao, General Garhan, pacification commissioner Yang Maoxun, and others led combined land and river forces to crush them at Douling; Hong Fu fled, and the supply route was reopened.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加一等。

translations.literal: When merit was reckoned, one degree was added to his rank.
translations.idiomatic: For this service his rank was raised one degree.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以捐俸賚軍賑難民，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for donating salary to provision the army and relieve refugees, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent for giving his salary to supply the army and relieve refugees.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進討來嘉、福，戰於房縣，獲其將五十二輩、印十二、劄牌二十四，遂克其城，進复保康。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he advanced to attack Jiajia and Fu, fought at Fangxian, captured fifty-two of their generals, twelve seals, and twenty-four tally-plaques, then took the city and further recovered Baokang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he marched against Yang Jiajia and Hong Fu, fought at Fangxian, captured fifty-two rebel officers, twelve seals, and twenty-four tally-plaques, took the city, and went on to recover Baokang.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與噶爾漢等攻興安，久而不下，命削戰陡嶺所敘加一等。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he and Garhan and others attacked Xing'an, which long would not fall; he was ordered stripped of the one degree added for the battle at Douling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he and Garhan besieged Xing'an without success for a long time, and the extra rank granted for Douling was taken back.

sentences.zh: 六月，授福建將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed General of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed general of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，諡忠愨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year and was posthumously titled Zhongmin (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封二等子。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, the fief was fixed as second-rank viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign the hereditary rank was fixed as second-class viscount.

sentences.zh: 達爾哈齊子養真，自有傳。

translations.literal: Darhachi's son Yangzhen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Darhachi's son Yangzhen has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李永芳，遼東鐵嶺人。

translations.literal: Li Yongfang was a native of Tieling in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yongfang was from Tieling in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 在明官撫順所游擊。

translations.literal: Under Ming he served as guerrilla commander of Fushun garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming he held the post of guerrilla commander at the Fushun garrison.

sentences.zh: 太祖克烏喇，烏喇貝勒布佔泰走葉赫。

translations.literal: When the Taizu conquered Ula, the Ula beile Buizhan fled to Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Ula, the Ula beile Buizhan fled to Yehe.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐葉赫，葉赫愬於明。

translations.literal: When the Taizu attacked Yehe, Yehe appealed to Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched against Yehe, Yehe appealed to the Ming court.

sentences.zh: 明使告太祖，誡毋侵葉赫。

translations.literal: Ming sent word to the Taizu, admonishing him not to invade Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: Ming sent envoys warning Taizu not to attack Yehe.

sentences.zh: 太祖以書與明，言葉赫渝盟悔婚，复匿布佔泰，不得已而用兵，躬詣撫順所，永芳迎三里外，導入教場，太祖出書畀永芳，乃引師還。

translations.literal: The Taizu wrote to Ming, saying Yehe had violated the alliance and repented the marriage, again harbored Buizhan, and had no choice but to use troops; he went in person to Fushun garrison; Yongfang met him three li outside and led him to the drill ground; the Taizu handed Yongfang the letter, then led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wrote to Ming that Yehe had broken its pact and repudiated a marriage alliance, was again sheltering Buizhan, and that he had been forced to take up arms; he went in person to Fushun, where Yongfang met him three li outside the post, escorted him to the drill ground, received the letter, and Taizu then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 後三歲為天命元年，又三歲，始用兵於明。

translations.literal: Three years later was the first year of Tianming; three years after that he first used troops against Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later came the first year of Tianming; three years after that he first opened hostilities against Ming.

sentences.zh: 四月甲辰昧爽，師至撫順所，遂合圍，執明兵一，使持書諭永芳曰：「明發兵疆外衛葉赫，我乃以師至。

translations.literal: On jiachen of the fourth month, at dawn, the army reached Fushun garrison, then closed the siege; one Ming soldier was seized to carry a letter instructing Yongfang: "Ming sent troops beyond the border to guard Yehe, and so I have come with my army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiachen of the fourth month the army reached Fushun and closed the siege; a Ming soldier was taken to bear a letter to Yongfang: "Because Ming sent troops beyond the frontier to shield Yehe, I have come with my army.

sentences.zh: 汝一游擊耳，戰亦豈能勝？

translations.literal: You are but a guerrilla commander—could you win in battle even if you fought?
translations.idiomatic: You are only a guerrilla commander—how could you hope to win in battle?

sentences.zh: 今諭汝降者：汝降，則我即日深入；

translations.literal: Now I instruct you on surrendering: if you surrender, I will on that same day press deep inward;
translations.idiomatic: Hear what surrender means: if you yield, I march deeper that very day;

sentences.zh: 汝不降，是誤我深入期也。

translations.literal: if you do not surrender, you delay the date for my deep advance.
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, you delay the day I was to advance inland.

sentences.zh: 汝多才智，識時務，我國方求才，稍足備任使，猶將舉而用之，與為婚媾；

translations.literal: You are full of talent and wisdom and know the times; our state is seeking talent, and if you are even slightly adequate for appointment we shall promote and employ you, and join you in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: You are clever and know which way the wind blows; our state is seeking men of ability, and if you are fit for office we shall raise and employ you and ally with you by marriage;

sentences.zh: 況如汝者有不加以寵榮與我一等大臣同列者乎？

translations.literal: moreover, would one such as you go without favor and glory, ranked with my foremost ministers?
translations.idiomatic: would a man like you not be honored and ranked with my highest ministers?

sentences.zh: 汝若欲戰，我矢豈能識汝？

translations.literal: If you wish to fight, could my arrows know you?
translations.idiomatic: If you choose to fight, can my arrows pick you out from the rest?

sentences.zh: 既不能勝，死復何益？

translations.literal: Since you cannot win, what use is death?
translations.idiomatic: Since you cannot win, what good is dying?

sentences.zh: 且汝出城降，我兵不復入，汝士卒皆安堵。

translations.literal: Moreover, if you leave the city to surrender, my soldiers will not enter again, and all your troops will live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: If you come out and surrender, my troops will not enter the city and your soldiers will remain unmolested.

sentences.zh: 若我師入城，男婦老弱必且驚潰，亦大不利於汝民矣。

translations.literal: If my army enters the city, the men, women, old and young will surely panic and scatter—which is also greatly to the harm of your people.
translations.idiomatic: If my army storms the walls, men, women, and children will panic and scatter—a great calamity for your people.

sentences.zh: 勿謂我恫喝，不可信也。

translations.literal: Do not say I am intimidating you—it is not to be disbelieved.
translations.idiomatic: Do not call this an empty threat—you may trust my word.

sentences.zh: 汝思區區一城且不能下，安用興師？

translations.literal: You reflect: if this petty city cannot be taken, what use to raise an army?
translations.idiomatic: Think: if I could not take this one small town, why would I raise an army at all?

sentences.zh: 失此弗圖，悔無及已。

translations.literal: Lose this and do not seize it—regret will never catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this chance and regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 降不降，汝熟計之。

translations.literal: Surrender or not—you reckon it well.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender or resist—weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 毋不忍一時之忿，違我言而僨事也！」

translations.literal: Do not bear a moment's wrath and go against my words and ruin the affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not let a moment's anger make you defy me and ruin everything!"

sentences.zh: 永芳得書，立城南門上請降，而仍令軍士備守具。

translations.literal: Yongfang received the letter and stood on the south gate requesting surrender, yet still ordered the troops to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfang read the letter and appeared on the south gate offering surrender, yet still had his men prepare to defend.

sentences.zh: 上命樹雲梯以攻，不移時，師登陴，斬守備王命印等。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered scaling ladders raised to attack; in no time the army mounted the wall, beheaded the garrison commander Wang Mingyin and others.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign ordered assault ladders raised; in no time his men were on the wall and beheaded the garrison commander Wang Mingyin and others.

sentences.zh: 永芳冠帶乘馬出降，固山額真阿敦引永芳下馬，匍匐謁上，上於馬上以禮答之，傳諭勿殺城中人。

translations.literal: Yongfang, capped and belted, came out on horseback to surrender; the Gushan Ejen Adun led Yongfang down from his horse; he crawled on his knees to pay homage; the sovereign from horseback returned the courtesy in ritual, and proclaimed that those in the city were not to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfang came out in full dress on horseback to surrender; Gushan Ejen Adun helped him dismount; he crawled forward to pay homage, and the sovereign answered him courteously from horseback and proclaimed that no one in the city was to be killed.

sentences.zh: 東州、馬根單二城及沿邊諸台堡五百餘，悉下。

translations.literal: Dongzhou, Magendan, and five hundred odd border platforms and fortresses all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhou, Magendan, and more than five hundred border forts and platforms all submitted.

sentences.zh: 是日，上駐撫順。

translations.literal: That day the sovereign halted at Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sovereign encamped at Fushun.

sentences.zh: 明日，命隳其城，乃還。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered the city demolished, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered the walls torn down and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 編降民千戶，遷之赫圖阿喇。

translations.literal: The surrendered population was organized into a thousand households and moved to Hetuala.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered people were organized into a thousand households and resettled at Hetuala.

sentences.zh: 命依明製設大小官屬，授永芳三等副將，轄其眾，以上第七子貝勒阿巴泰女妻焉。

translations.literal: He ordered officials great and small set up according to Ming institutions; Yongfang was made third-rank deputy general to command his people; the sovereign's seventh son, Prince Abatai, was given a daughter to marry him.
translations.idiomatic: Offices great and small were established on the Ming model; Yongfang was made third-rank deputy general over his followers, and a daughter of the sovereign's seventh son, Prince Abatai, was given him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐明取邊城，自撫順始；

translations.literal: The Taizu's campaigns against Ming to take border cities began with Fushun;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's conquest of Ming border towns began with Fushun;

sentences.zh: 明邊將降太祖，亦自永芳始。

translations.literal: Ming border generals who surrendered to the Taizu also began with Yongfang.
translations.idiomatic: and Ming border generals who went over to Taizu also began with Yongfang.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，上复伐明，拔清河。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month the sovereign again attacked Ming and took Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the seventh month, the sovereign again attacked Ming and took Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 四年，克鐵嶺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he captured Tieling.

sentences.zh: 六年，下遼、瀋。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he took Liaoyang and Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he took Liaoyang and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 永芳皆從，以功授三等總兵官。

translations.literal: Yongfang followed in all these campaigns; for his merit he was appointed third-rank commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfang took part in all of them and, for his service, was made a third-rank commander.

sentences.zh: 明巡撫王化貞及諸邊將屢遣諜招永芳，永芳輒執奏，上嘉獎，敕免死三次。

translations.literal: Ming grand coordinator Wang Huazhen and various border generals repeatedly sent agents to win Yongfang over; Yongfang always seized them and memorialized the sovereign, who praised and rewarded him and decreed three exemptions from the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming grand coordinator Wang Huazhen and other frontier generals repeatedly sent spies to win Yongfang over, but Yongfang always seized them and reported to the throne; the sovereign praised him and granted three exemptions from the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以朝鮮與明將毛文龍相應援，納逋逃，命貝勒阿敏等帥師討之，永芳從。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, because Joseon was coordinating with the Ming general Mao Wenlong and sheltering fugitives, he ordered princes Amin and others to lead troops to chastise them; Yongfang accompanied the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong came to the throne, Joseon's coordination with the Ming general Mao Wenlong and its sheltering of fugitives prompted him to send Prince Amin and others against Korea; Yongfang went with them.

sentences.zh: 上諭阿敏等曰：「朝鮮理當討，然非必欲取之。

translations.literal: The sovereign instructed Amin and the others: "Joseon ought properly to be chastised, yet it is not that we necessarily wish to take it.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign told Amin and the others: "Korea deserves chastisement, but we do not necessarily mean to conquer it.

sentences.zh: 凡事相機度義而行。」

translations.literal: In all matters act according to the opportunity and weigh what is right."
translations.idiomatic: In everything, act as circumstances and principle require."

sentences.zh: 克義州，分兵攻鐵山，擊走文龍；

translations.literal: They took Uiju, divided forces to attack Tieshan, and routed Wenlong;
translations.idiomatic: They captured Uiju, sent detachments against Tieshan, and drove off Wenlong;

sentences.zh: 進下定州、安州，次平壤，其官民皆遁，遂渡大同江。

translations.literal: advanced to take Jeongju and Anju, then encamped at Pyongyang; its officials and people all fled, and they crossed the Daedong River.
translations.idiomatic: then took Jeongju and Anju and halted at Pyongyang, whose officials and people had all fled; they crossed the Daedong River.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮王李倧使齎書迎師，諸貝勒答書歷數其罪，許以遣大臣蒞盟，當班師。

translations.literal: King Injo of Joseon sent envoys bearing letters to welcome the army; the princes replied listing his offenses and promised that if he sent ministers to come and conclude an alliance they would withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: King Injo of Joseon sent envoys with letters welcoming the army; the princes answered with a bill of his crimes and promised that if he sent ministers to swear alliance, they would withdraw.

sentences.zh: 使既行，師復進，次黃州，倧使馳告已遣大臣蒞盟。

translations.literal: After the envoys departed, the army advanced again and halted at Hwangju; Injo sent a fast messenger to say he had already dispatched ministers to come and conclude an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoys had gone, the army pushed on again and stopped at Hwangju, where Injo sent word by fast courier that ministers were already on their way to swear alliance.

sentences.zh: 阿敏欲遂攻其都城，諸貝勒謂宜待所遣大臣至，永芳進曰：「我等奉上命，仗義而行。

translations.literal: Amin wanted to proceed at once to attack the capital; the princes said they ought to wait until the ministers sent arrived. Yongfang stepped forward and said: "We received the sovereign's command and act by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Amin wanted to press on and attack the capital, but the princes argued they should wait for the promised ministers. Yongfang stepped forward and said: "We carry out the sovereign's orders and act in good faith.

sentences.zh: 前與朝鮮書，許以遣大臣蒞盟當班師，今食言不義。

translations.literal: In our earlier letter to Joseon we promised that if they sent ministers to come and conclude an alliance we would withdraw; to break our word now would be unrighteous.
translations.idiomatic: In our earlier letter to Korea we promised that if ministers came to swear alliance we would withdraw; to break that promise would be dishonorable.

sentences.zh: 盍暫駐待之？」

translations.literal: Why not halt briefly and wait for them?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not halt here and wait for them?"

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒皆是其言，阿敏怒，叱永芳曰：「爾蠻奴，何多言！

translations.literal: The princes all agreed with his words. Amin grew angry and shouted at Yongfang: "You barbarian slave—why so much talk!
translations.idiomatic: The princes all agreed with him. Amin flew into a rage and shouted at Yongfang: "You barbarian slave—why so many words!

sentences.zh: 我豈不能殺爾耶？」

translations.literal: Can I not kill you?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I cannot kill you?"

sentences.zh: 師再進，次平山，倧所遣大臣至師，卒如永芳議，遣劉興祚、庫爾纏如倧所，蒞盟而還。

translations.literal: The army advanced again and halted at Pyeongsan; the ministers Injo had sent reached the army, and in the end, as Yongfang had urged, Liu Xingzuo and Kuerchan were sent to Injo's court to conclude the alliance, then they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced again and stopped at Pyeongsan; Injo's ministers reached camp, and in the end, as Yongfang had urged, Liu Xingzuo and Kuerchan were sent to Injo's court to swear alliance before the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八年，永芳卒，有子九人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Yongfang died, leaving nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Yongfang died, survived by nine sons.

sentences.zh: 漢軍旗制定，隸正藍旗漢軍。

translations.literal: When the Han Eight Banners were fixed, his line was placed in the Plain Blue Banner Han division.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han Eight Banners were established, his family was registered in the Plain Blue Banner Han corps.

sentences.zh: 次子李率泰，自有傳。

translations.literal: His second son Li Shuaite has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Li Shuaite, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 第三子剛阿泰，順治初，官宣府總兵。

translations.literal: The third son Gangatai, at the beginning of the Shunzhi reign, was made Xuande-fu garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, Gangatai, was appointed garrison commander of Xuande-fu at the start of the Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 時姜瓖為亂，山西北境諸州縣土寇蜂起，瓖既平，所部竄匿代州、定襄、繁峙五台山中。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Xiang was in rebellion; local bandits sprang up in the northern prefectures and counties of Shanxi. After Jiang was pacified, his remnant followers hid in the Wutai Mountains among Daizhou, Dingxiang, and Fanshi.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiang Xiang was in revolt, local bandits rose across northern Shanxi; after Jiang was crushed, his scattered followers took refuge in the Wutai Mountains around Daizhou, Dingxiang, and Fanshi.

sentences.zh: 剛阿泰先後逐捕，諸山砦悉平。

translations.literal: Gangatai pursued and captured them in successive operations, and all the mountain strongholds were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gangatai hunted them down in successive campaigns until every mountain stronghold was cleared.

sentences.zh: 旋以屬吏侵餉劾罷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached and dismissed because a subordinate had embezzled military rations.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon impeached and removed from office after a subordinate was found to have embezzled pay and provisions.

sentences.zh: 第五子巴顏，天聰八年襲父爵，例改三等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: The fifth son Bayan, in the eighth year of Tiancong, inherited his father's title, which by regulation was changed to third-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son, Bayan, inherited his father's rank in the eighth year of Tiancong; by regulation it was converted to third-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 崇德間，以參領從太宗徵科爾沁；

translations.literal: During the Chongde period, as a staff colonel he followed Taizong in campaigning against the Khorchin;
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongde era he served as a staff colonel under Taizong in the campaign against the Khorchin;

sentences.zh: 圍錦州，與洪承疇戰松山城下：皆有功。

translations.literal: at the siege of Jinzhou and in fighting Hong Chengchou below Songshan—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: at the siege of Jinzhou and in the battle with Hong Chengchou below Songshan—distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 七年，定漢軍八旗，以巴顏為正藍旗固山額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Han Eight Banners were established, Bayan was made Gushan Ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Han Eight Banners were fixed, Bayan was appointed Gushan Ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗等徵寧遠，拔中後所、前屯衛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year he followed Prince Cheng Jirhalang and others in campaigning against Ningyuan and took Zhonghousuo and Qiantunwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year he joined Prince Cheng Jirhalang and others against Ningyuan and captured Zhonghousuo and Qiantunwei.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，進二等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was promoted to second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was raised to second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 旋與固山額真石廷柱剿寇昌平，與固山額真葉臣徇直隸饒陽，河南懷慶，山西澤州、潞安諸府縣，師還，賜白金五百。

translations.literal: He then joined Gushan Ejen Shi Tingzhu in suppressing bandits at Changping, and with Gushan Ejen Yechen swept Raoyang in Zhili, Huaiqing in Henan, and Zezhou, Lu'an, and other prefectures and counties in Shanxi; when the army returned he was granted five hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: He then worked with Gushan Ejen Shi Tingzhu to suppress bandits at Changping, and with Gushan Ejen Yechen swept Raoyang in Zhili, Huaiqing in Henan, and Zezhou, Lu'an, and other counties in Shanxi; on returning from campaign he received five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 二年，從定西大將軍和洛輝自陝西徇四川，流寇孫守法、賀珍犯西安，再戰大破之，逐至黑水峪，斬守法；

translations.literal: In the second year he followed the Pacifier of the West Grand General Heluo Hui from Shaanxi into Sichuan; the bandit leaders Sun Shoufa and He Zhen attacked Xi'an; in two battles he smashed them, pursued them to Heishuiyu, and beheaded Shoufa;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he followed Grand General Heluo Hui, Pacifier of the West, from Shaanxi into Sichuan; when the bandits Sun Shoufa and He Zhen struck at Xi'an, he routed them in two battles, pursued them to Heishuiyu, and killed Shoufa;

sentences.zh: 又破流寇一隻虎於商州，克延安諸路山寨。

translations.literal: he again defeated the bandit Yizhihu at Shangzhou and captured the mountain strongholds along the Yan'an routes.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the bandit Yizhihu at Shangzhou and took the mountain strongholds throughout the Yan'an region.

sentences.zh: 四年，例改二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, by regulation his title was changed to second-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his title was converted by regulation to second-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.

sentences.zh: 五年，進一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to first-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was raised to first-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.

sentences.zh: 討叛將薑瓖，從睿親王多爾袞复渾源州；

translations.literal: In suppressing the rebel general Jiang Xiang, he followed Prince Rui Dorgon in recovering Hunyuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the rebel Jiang Xiang he followed Prince Rui Dorgon in retaking Hunyuanzhou;

sentences.zh: 從英親王阿濟格复左衛；

translations.literal: followed Prince Ying Ajige in recovering Zuowei;
translations.idiomatic: followed Prince Ying Ajige in retaking Zuowei;

sentences.zh: 從巽親王滿達海復朔州、汾州及太谷諸縣。

translations.literal: and followed Prince Xun Manduhai in recovering Shuozhou, Fenzhou, Taigu, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: and followed Prince Xun Manduhai in retaking Shuozhou, Fenzhou, Taigu, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 巴顏在軍將左翼，挾火器以攻，所向皆克。

translations.literal: In the army Bayan commanded the left wing, attacking with firearms; wherever he went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In the field Bayan led the left wing, attacking with firearms, and carried every position he assaulted.

sentences.zh: 八年，敘平姜瓖功，复遇恩詔，進一等伯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, in recognition of merit in pacifying Jiang Xiang and again upon a grace edict, he was promoted to first-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his service in crushing Jiang Xiang was rewarded, and on a further grace edict he was raised to first-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，定封號曰昭信。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period his title was fixed as Zhaoxin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong his hereditary title was fixed as Zhaoxin.

sentences.zh: 四十年正月，命以其族改隸鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fortieth year an order was issued that his clan be transferred to the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fortieth year his entire clan was ordered transferred to the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 石廷柱，遼東人。

translations.literal: Shi Tingzhu was a native of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tingzhu was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 先世居蘇完，姓瓜爾佳氏。

translations.literal: His forebears had dwelt at Suwan and bore the clan name Guwalgiya.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors lived at Suwan and belonged to the Guwalgiya clan.

sentences.zh: 明成化間，有布哈者，為建州左衛指揮。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign of Ming there was one Buha who served as commander of the Jianzhou Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua era of Ming, a man named Buha served as commander of the Jianzhou Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 布哈生阿爾松阿，嘉靖中襲職。

translations.literal: Buha begot Arsungga; in the Jiajing period the latter succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Buha's son Arsungga inherited the post during the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 阿爾松阿生石翰，移家遼東，遂以「石」為氏。

translations.literal: Arsungga begot Shi Han, who moved his household to Liaodong and then took "Shi" as the surname.
translations.idiomatic: Arsungga's son Shi Han moved the family to Liaodong and adopted "Shi" as the surname.

sentences.zh: 石翰子三：國柱、天柱、廷柱。

translations.literal: Shi Han had three sons: Guozhu, Tianzhu, and Tingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Han had three sons: Guozhu, Tianzhu, and Tingzhu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆之季，廷柱為廣寧守備，天柱為千總。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wanli reign Tingzhu was garrison commandant of Guangning and Tianzhu was a company captain.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wanli era Tingzhu was garrison commandant of Guangning and Tianzhu a company captain.

sentences.zh: 太祖師至，巡撫王化貞走入關，天柱先與諸生郭肇基出謁，且曰：「吾曹已守城門矣。」

translations.literal: When Taizu's army arrived, Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen fled through the pass into the interior; Tianzhu first went out with the licentiate Guo Zhaoji to meet them and said: "We have already secured the city gates."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu's army arrived, Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen fled through the pass; Tianzhu went out first with the licentiate Guo Zhaoji to meet them and said: "We have already secured the city gates."

sentences.zh: 翌日入城，廷柱從眾降，授世職游擊，俾轄降眾。

translations.literal: The next day they entered the city; Tingzhu followed the multitude in surrendering, was appointed hereditary guerrilla commander, and was charged with overseeing those who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they entered the city; Tingzhu surrendered with the rest, was given the hereditary rank of guerrilla commander, and put in charge of the surrendered troops.

sentences.zh: 蒙古巴林部貝勒囊努克背盟劫掠，廷柱從上討之，取其寨，收牲畜以還，進三等副將。

translations.literal: When the Mongol Balin prince Nangnuk broke the alliance and raided, Tingzhu followed the sovereign to chastise him, took his stockade, gathered livestock and returned, and was promoted to third-rank deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: When the Balin Mongol prince Nangnuk broke the alliance and raided, Tingzhu joined the sovereign's punitive expedition, seized his camp, drove off the livestock, and was promoted to third-rank deputy general.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，太宗命率兵搜剿明故毛文龍所轄諸島，敵自石城島來犯，擊斬二百人，俘十九人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong Taizong ordered him to lead troops to search out and suppress the islands formerly under Ming's Mao Wenlong; the enemy came from Shicheng Island to attack; he killed two hundred and captured nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancong Taizong sent him to sweep the islands once held by the Ming general Mao Wenlong; when the enemy attacked from Shicheng Island he killed two hundred men and took nineteen prisoners.

sentences.zh: 尋從上伐明，薄明都。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the sovereign in attacking Ming and drew near the Ming capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the sovereign against Ming and pressed close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，師還，至沙河驛，廷柱與達海諭城中軍民出降；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, as the army returned and reached Shahe Post, Tingzhu and Dahai urged the soldiers and civilians in the city to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the return march at Shahe Post, Tingzhu and Dahai persuaded the city's soldiers and civilians to surrender;

sentences.zh: 又與達海以千人诇漢兒莊，漢兒莊與三屯營、喜峰口諸堡先已降而复叛，至是復降。

translations.literal: again, with Dahai and a thousand men he reconnoitered Han'erzhuang; Han'erzhuang, together with Santunying, Xifengkou, and other forts, had previously submitted and then rebelled again—they now submitted once more.
translations.idiomatic: he and Dahai then reconnoitered Han'erzhuang with a thousand men; Han'erzhuang, Santunying, Xifengkou, and other forts that had submitted and rebelled now surrendered again.

sentences.zh: 五年，明總兵祖大壽築城大凌河，上自將圍之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ming commander Zu Dashou fortified Dalinghe; the sovereign personally led the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Ming commander Zu Dashou fortified Dalinghe, and the sovereign personally led the siege.

sentences.zh: 大壽窮蹙，使從子澤潤射書請降，並乞上令廷柱往議。

translations.literal: Dashou, hard pressed, had his nephew Zerun shoot in a letter requesting surrender and also begged that the sovereign send Tingzhu to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Dashou had his nephew Zerun shoot in a letter offering surrender and asked that the sovereign send Tingzhu to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 廷柱與達海至城南，先使薑桂诇大壽，桂故明千總，為我軍所俘。

translations.literal: Tingzhu and Dahai reached the south of the city and first sent Jiang Gui to spy out Dashou; Gui had formerly been a Ming company captain and had been captured by our army.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu and Dahai reached the south wall and first sent Jiang Gui, a former Ming company captain now in Qing hands, to sound out Dashou.

sentences.zh: 大壽使游擊韓棟從桂出迎廷柱，並以其義子可法為質。

translations.literal: Dashou sent Guerrilla Commander Han Dong with Gui to meet Tingzhu, and also sent his adopted son Kefa as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou sent Guerrilla Commander Han Dong out with Gui to receive Tingzhu and offered his adopted son Kefa as hostage.

sentences.zh: 廷柱乃逾壕與語，大壽言決降，惟乞速取錦州，俾妻子得相見。

translations.literal: Tingzhu then crossed the moat to speak with him; Dashou declared his firm intent to surrender but only begged that Jinzhou be taken quickly so that he and his wife and children might meet.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu crossed the moat to parley; Dashou declared he would surrender, but begged that Jinzhou be taken quickly so he could be reunited with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 廷柱以告，上復遣廷柱諭指，大壽乃降。

translations.literal: Tingzhu reported this; the sovereign again sent Tingzhu to explain the terms, and Dashou then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu reported back, the sovereign sent him again to state the terms, and Dashou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是時佟養性為烏真超哈昂邦章京，廷柱為副。

translations.literal: At this time Tong Yangxing was Angbang Zhangjing of the Ujencooha and Tingzhu was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tong Yangxing was Angbang Zhangjing of the Ujencooha, with Tingzhu as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 六年，養性卒，廷柱代為昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yangxing died and Tingzhu succeeded him as Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Yangxing died, and Tingzhu took his place as Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 從伐察哈爾，多斬獲。

translations.literal: Following a campaign against the Chahar, he made many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Chahar and won many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 七年，從貝勒岳託伐明，攻旅順，師還，上酌金卮以勞，進三等總兵官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Prince Yue Tuo in attacking Ming and assaulting Lüshun; when the army returned the sovereign poured wine from a golden goblet to reward him, and he was promoted to third-rank commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Prince Yue Tuo against Ming and assaulted Lüshun; on the army's return the sovereign rewarded him from a golden goblet and promoted him to third-rank commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，從伐明，攻應州，克石家村堡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in attacking Ming, assaulted Yingzhou, and took the Shijia Village fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the Ming campaign, attacked Yingzhou, and captured Shijia Village fort.

sentences.zh: 九年，復從伐明，與明兵戰大凌河西，斬明副將劉應選，獲游擊曹得功等。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again followed in attacking Ming, fought Ming troops west of Dalinghe, beheaded Ming vice commander Liu Yingxuan, and captured Guerrilla Commander Cao Degong and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again campaigned against Ming, fought west of Dalinghe, killed the Ming vice commander Liu Yingxuan, and captured Guerrilla Commander Cao Degong and others.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，上自將伐朝鮮，命廷柱帥所部整兵械，儲糗崿，挾火器以從。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde the sovereign personally led a campaign against Joseon and ordered Tingzhu to lead his unit in preparing arms, storing rations, and bringing firearms along.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde the sovereign personally invaded Korea and ordered Tingzhu to ready his troops, stock provisions, and bring firearms.

sentences.zh: 二年，既定朝鮮，還攻皮島，廷柱與戶部承政馬福塔攻其北隅。

translations.literal: In the second year, after Joseon was settled, he returned to attack Pidao; Tingzhu and Board of Revenue Chancellor Ma Futa assaulted its northern corner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after Korea was pacified, he turned to attack Pidao; Tingzhu and Board of Revenue Chancellor Ma Futa struck its northern flank.

sentences.zh: 尋追論朝鮮王李倧謁上時廷柱亂班釋甲，及縱士卒違法妄行罪，解任，罰鍰，奪賞賚。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, revisiting the offenses of Tingzhu's breaking ranks and removing his armor when King Injo of Joseon paid homage to the sovereign, and of his allowing soldiers to act lawlessly, he was removed from office, fined, and stripped of awards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon punished for breaking ranks and doffing his armor when King Injo paid homage, and for letting his men act lawlessly—removed from office, fined, and stripped of rewards.

sentences.zh: 是年分烏真超哈為左、右翼，以廷柱為左翼固山額真。

translations.literal: That year the Ujencooha was divided into left and right wings; Tingzhu was made Gushan Ejen of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ujencooha was split into left and right wings, and Tingzhu was appointed Gushan Ejen of the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 三年，上與諸臣論兵事，舉呂尚相勗，廷柱言：「呂尚制閫外專生殺，故所向有功。

translations.literal: In the third year the sovereign discussed military affairs with his ministers and cited Lü Shang as encouragement; Tingzhu said: "Lü Shang held sole authority over life and death beyond the pass, so wherever he went he succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, as the sovereign discussed military affairs with his ministers and held up Lü Shang as a model, Tingzhu said: "Lü Shang held sole power of life and death outside the capital, and so he always prevailed.

sentences.zh: 今臣等若有過下部逮訊，雖牛錄以下亦當比肩對簿，其何以堪？」

translations.literal: If we now err and the lower ministries arrest and interrogate us, even men below the niru rank must stand shoulder to shoulder at the docket—how can we bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: If we err today and the lower ministries arrest us for questioning, even men below the niru rank must stand side by side in court—how can we endure that?"

sentences.zh: 諸臣以其言戇，請下刑部議罪論死，上命宥之。

translations.literal: The ministers regarded his words as rash and asked that he be sent to the Board of Punishments to deliberate guilt and sentence to death; the sovereign ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers thought his words reckless and asked that he be sent to the Board of Punishments for trial and a death sentence; the sovereign pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，從伐明，攻錦州，克城外諸屯堡，進破城旁台。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month he followed in attacking Ming, assaulted Jinzhou, took the stockaded villages outside the walls, and advanced to destroy a platform beside the city.
translations.idiomatic: That October he joined the Ming campaign, attacked Jinzhou, captured the stockaded villages outside the walls, and destroyed a nearby platform.

sentences.zh: 台上餘敵兵潛自間道走，廷柱弗追擊，部議降爵罰鍰，上復命宥之。

translations.literal: The remaining enemy on the platform slipped away by a hidden path; Tingzhu did not pursue; the ministry proposed reducing his rank and fining him, but the sovereign again ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors on the platform escaped by a hidden path; Tingzhu did not pursue. The ministry proposed demotion and a fine, but the sovereign pardoned him again.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，上自將伐明，烏真超哈諸將孔有德、耿仲明、尚可喜、馬光遠及廷柱皆率所部從。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the sovereign personally led a campaign against Ming; the Ujencooha generals Kong Youde, Geng Zhongming, Shang Kexi, Ma Guangyuan, and Tingzhu all led their units along.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year the sovereign personally campaigned against Ming; the Ujencooha generals Kong Youde, Geng Zhongming, Shang Kexi, Ma Guangyuan, and Tingzhu all led their troops with him.

sentences.zh: 上駐軍松山，命廷柱攻城南台，毀其堞，台兵不能禦，守將王昌功等四十餘人出降。

translations.literal: The sovereign encamped at Songshan and ordered Tingzhu to attack the south platform, destroy its parapet; the platform troops could not resist; garrison commander Wang Changgong and more than forty others came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign encamped at Songshan and ordered Tingzhu to take the south platform; he smashed its parapet, the defenders could not hold, and garrison commander Wang Changgong and more than forty others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 上登松山南岡度地形，命廷柱從。

translations.literal: The sovereign climbed the southern ridge of Songshan to survey the terrain and ordered Tingzhu to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign climbed the southern ridge of Songshan to survey the ground and had Tingzhu accompany him.

sentences.zh: 可喜以砲攻城南門之左，廷柱與光遠先取城西南隅台，諸將繼進，攻城，城堞皆盡，會以日暮罷。

translations.literal: Kexi bombarded the left of the south gate with cannon; Tingzhu and Guangyuan first took the southwest corner platform; the other generals pressed on in succession to assault the city until the parapets were all gone; they halted when night fell.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi shelled the left flank of the south gate; Tingzhu and Guangyuan first seized the southwest corner platform; the other generals pressed the assault until the parapets were gone, then broke off at dusk.

sentences.zh: 明日攻益急，城兵守禦甚固，我兵緣雲梯上不能入，死者二十餘人，廷柱兄子達爾漢亦被創。

translations.literal: The next day the assault grew fiercer; the city troops defended very stoutly; our men climbed scaling ladders but could not enter; more than twenty died, and Tingzhu's brother's son Darhan was also wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the attack intensified; the defenders held firm; our men mounted scaling ladders but could not break in; more than twenty were killed, and Tingzhu's nephew Darhan was wounded.

sentences.zh: 上召詢諸將，皆謂攻必克。

translations.literal: The sovereign summoned and questioned the generals; all said the assault would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign called the generals in and asked their view; all said the city would surely fall.

sentences.zh: 翌日復集議，有德、仲明、可喜、光遠欲鑿地道以攻，廷柱持不可。

translations.literal: The next day they met again; Youde, Zhongming, Kexi, and Guangyuan wished to tunnel to attack, but Tingzhu held that this would not do.
translations.idiomatic: They met again the next day; Youde, Zhongming, Kexi, and Guangyuan wanted to tunnel under the walls, but Tingzhu objected.

sentences.zh: 上責廷柱曰：「爾為主將，恇怯無鬥志，與諸將異議。

translations.literal: The sovereign rebuked Tingzhu: "You are the chief commander—timid and without fighting spirit, at odds with the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign rebuked Tingzhu: "You are the chief commander—timid and spiritless, at odds with the other generals.

sentences.zh: 爾豈因兄子被創，故驚怖不欲戰耶？」

translations.literal: Is it because your brother's son was wounded that you are frightened and unwilling to fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you frightened and unwilling to fight because your nephew was wounded?"

sentences.zh: 廷柱惶恐，對曰：「臣昔嘗巡邏至此，知地中有水石不可穿，且亦不能越壕而過，故不敢不言。

translations.literal: Tingzhu, alarmed, replied: "Your servant once patrolled to this place and knows that water and stone lie under the ground and cannot be pierced, and that one also cannot cross the moat that way—therefore I dared not remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Tingzhu replied: "Your servant once patrolled here and knows the ground is full of water and stone and cannot be tunneled, and that one cannot cross the moat that way—I dared not keep silent.

sentences.zh: 今眾皆謂可攻，臣焉敢獨異？」

translations.literal: Now all say it can be attacked—how could I alone differ?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that all say it can be done, how could I alone dissent?"

sentences.zh: 乃與有德等鳩役於城南鑿地道。

translations.literal: He then joined Youde and the others in pressing laborers to dig a tunnel south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Youde and the others in pressing laborers to dig a tunnel south of the city.

sentences.zh: 初，祖大壽既降，請得入錦州，乃復叛，為明守；

translations.literal: At the outset Zu Dashou, having surrendered, asked to be allowed to enter Jinzhou, then rebelled again and held it for Ming;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zu Dashou had surrendered and asked to be allowed into Jinzhou, then rebelled again and held it for Ming;

sentences.zh: 至是，聞松山急，遣蒙古兵三百乘夜入城，诇得我軍謀，多為備，地道不能達，乃罷攻。

translations.literal: at this juncture, hearing that Songshan was in crisis, he sent three hundred Mongol troops by night into the city; they learned our army's plan; the defenders took many precautions; the tunnel could not reach its goal, and the assault was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Now, hearing Songshan was hard pressed, he sent three hundred Mongol troops into the city by night; they learned of our tunnel plan, the defenders made ready, the tunnel failed to reach the wall, and the assault was called off.

sentences.zh: 師還，部議廷柱攻城不盡力，當罷任罰鍰，上仍命宥之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the ministry proposed that Tingzhu had not exerted himself fully in the siege and ought to be removed and fined; the sovereign again ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the ministry proposed that Tingzhu had not fought hard enough and should be removed and fined; the sovereign pardoned him again.

sentences.zh: 時烏真超哈复析為八旗，合二旗為一固山，於是漢軍旗制始定。

translations.literal: At that time the Ujencooha was again divided into Eight Banners, with two banners combined into one gushan; thus the Han Banner system was first established.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ujencooha was reorganized into Eight Banners, two banners to each gushan, and the Han Banner system was fixed.

sentences.zh: 廷柱隸正白旗。

translations.literal: Tingzhu was placed in the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu was registered in the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，廷柱上言：「錦州為遼左首鎮，我師築壘浚壕，誓必翦滅，以策進取，誠至計也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year Tingzhu memorialized: "Jinzhou is the chief fortress of eastern Liaodong; our army is building fortifications and digging trenches, vowing to destroy it utterly as a strategy for advance—this is indeed the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year Tingzhu memorialized: "Jinzhou is the chief fortress of eastern Liaodong; our army is entrenching and vowing to destroy it as the key to further advance—a sound strategy indeed.

sentences.zh: 第明恃大壽為保障，我師圍之急，彼必益發援兵，並力一戰。

translations.literal: But Ming relies on Dashou as its bulwark; if our army presses the siege, they will surely send more relief troops and join forces for a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: But Ming relies on Dashou as its shield; the tighter we press the siege, the more relief they will send for a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 宜及此時簡精銳，分佈各旗屯田所，遇警即並進。

translations.literal: We ought at this time to select crack troops, station them at the garrison-farm sites of each banner, and when alarm comes advance together at once.
translations.idiomatic: We should now pick elite troops and station them at each banner's garrison-farm posts so they can march out together at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 如敵已立營，以砲環擊，伺其稍動，我師即突起乘之，轉戰過錦州，至松山、杏山間，敵必敗走，則錦州破矣。

translations.literal: If the enemy has already encamped, ring them with cannon fire; when they stir slightly our army should rise at once and strike; fighting past Jinzhou to between Songshan and Xingshan, the enemy will surely break and flee—and Jinzhou will fall.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy has already encamped, surround them with artillery; when they stir, our troops should strike at once, fight past Jinzhou to the ground between Songshan and Xingshan, the enemy will break and flee, and Jinzhou will fall.

sentences.zh: 錦州既破，關外八城聞而震動。

translations.literal: Once Jinzhou is taken, the eight cities beyond the pass will hear of it and be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinzhou falls, the eight cities beyond the pass will hear of it and tremble.

sentences.zh: 昔年克瀋陽，遼陽從之下；

translations.literal: Years ago when Shenyang was taken, Liaoyang followed in submission;
translations.idiomatic: In years past, when Shenyang fell, Liaoyang submitted in turn;

sentences.zh: 克沙嶺，廣寧亦從之下。

translations.literal: when Shaling was taken, Guangning also followed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: when Shaling was taken, Guangning followed as well.

sentences.zh: 此其明徵也。

translations.literal: This is clear evidence of it.
translations.idiomatic: That is clear proof.

sentences.zh: 近聞喀爾喀扎薩克圖揚言取歸化，恐陰欲取鄂爾多斯。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that the Khalkha Zasagtu Khan openly declares he will take Guihua; I fear he secretly intends to seize Ordos as well.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that the Khalkha Zasagtu Khan openly vows to take Guihua, and I fear he secretly aims at Ordos as well.

sentences.zh: 臣擬令鄂爾多斯移牧黃河南，使與歸化相接，彼此策應。

translations.literal: Your subject proposes ordering Ordos to move pastures south of the Yellow River, causing them to adjoin Guihua and to plan mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that Ordos be moved to pasture south of the Yellow River, adjoining Guihua so the two can cover each other.

sentences.zh: 仍選才勇將士挾火器戍焉，而令王貝勒帥師道宣、大，略應州、雁門。

translations.literal: Still select capable and brave officers carrying firearms to garrison there, and order Prince Wang and the beile to lead troops by way of Xuan and Da, sweeping Yingzhou and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Select able and brave officers with firearms to garrison the area, and have Prince Wang and the beile lead troops via Xuanfu and Datong to sweep Yingzhou and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 歸化有警，輕騎倍道赴援。

translations.literal: If Guihua is alarmed, light cavalry should go by forced marches to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: If Guihua comes under attack, light cavalry should ride by forced marches to its relief.

sentences.zh: 明所恃為遼東援者，不過宣大、陝西榆林、甘肅寧夏諸路。

translations.literal: The forces Ming relies on to relieve Liaodong are no more than the routes of Xuan-Da, Yulin in Shaanxi, and Ningxia in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's relief for Liaodong depends on no more than the Xuan-Da route, Yulin in Shaanxi, and Ningxia in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 我師西入，諸路自顧不遑，豈能復出援遼哉？

translations.literal: If our army enters from the west, those routes will be too busy defending themselves—how could they again march out to relieve Liaodong?
translations.idiomatic: If our army strikes westward, those routes will be hard pressed to defend themselves—how could they march out again to save Liaodong?

sentences.zh: 此一舉而兩得也。

translations.literal: With one move we gain two advantages.
translations.idiomatic: One stroke would secure a double gain.

sentences.zh: 明援兵自寧遠至松山，所齎行糧不過六七日，其鋒少挫，勢必速退；

translations.literal: Ming relief troops from Ningyuan to Songshan carry marching rations for no more than six or seven days; if their spearhead is even slightly blunted, they will surely withdraw quickly;
translations.idiomatic: Ming relief from Ningyuan to Songshan carries rations for scarcely six or seven days; once their vanguard is checked, they will surely pull back at once;

sentences.zh: 即宿留數日，終且託糧盡而返。

translations.literal: Even if they linger several days, in the end they will plead exhausted rations and return.
translations.idiomatic: even if they stay a few days longer, in the end they will claim their grain is spent and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 宜設伏於高橋險★C7處，鑿壕截擊，仍發勁兵綴其後，使進退無路，則彼援兵皆折而降我矣。

translations.literal: Ambushes should be set at high bridges and narrow defiles, trenches dug to intercept and strike, and crack troops still sent to hang on their rear so they have no way forward or back—then those relief troops will all break and surrender to us.
translations.idiomatic: Set ambushes at high bridges and narrow passes, dig trenches to cut them off, and send crack troops to cling to their rear until they can neither advance nor retreat—then their relief force will break and surrender to us.

sentences.zh: 我師遇敵步兵，每奮勇陷陣，彼軍多火器，恐致傷夷。

translations.literal: When our army meets enemy infantry we always charge boldly into their ranks, but their army has many firearms, and I fear this will cause casualties among our men.
translations.idiomatic: Our men always charge boldly when they meet enemy foot soldiers, but the Ming force is heavy with firearms, and I fear we will suffer needless losses.

sentences.zh: 宜诇敵遠離城郭，或憑據高阜，水竭糧匱，乃環而攻之。

translations.literal: We should scout until the enemy is far from towns and walls, or has taken a high hill with water exhausted and provisions spent, and only then surround and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: We should wait until the enemy is far from walled towns, or has taken a high hill with water gone and grain spent, and only then surround and attack.

sentences.zh: 夜則鑿壕以守，晝則發砲以擊。

translations.literal: By night dig trenches to hold the line; by day open cannon fire to strike.
translations.idiomatic: By night we should dig trenches and hold our ground; by day open cannon fire on them.

sentences.zh: 不一二日，勢且生變，其斃可坐俟也。

translations.literal: In a day or two their situation will surely change, and their destruction can be awaited seated.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day or two their situation will turn, and their ruin can be awaited without stirring.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇書生耳，所統援遼諸鎮，皆烏合亡命，外張聲勢，內實恇懾。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou is a mere scholar; the garrisons he commands for Liaodong relief are all a rabble of desperate men—outwardly they bluster, inwardly they are truly timid.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou is only a scholar; the Liaodong relief garrisons under him are a mob of desperate men who bluster outwardly but are inwardly terrified.

sentences.zh: 如大壽為我師所破，承疇與諸將縱得脫去，亦東市就僇而已。

translations.literal: If Dashou is broken by our army, even if Chengchou and the other generals escape, they will only go to the execution ground at Dongshi.
translations.idiomatic: If Dashou is broken by our army, even should Chengchou and his generals escape, they will only face execution at Dongshi.

sentences.zh: 彼聞上恩豢降將，或慕義納款，亦未可料。

translations.literal: When they hear how generously the sovereign nourishes surrendered generals, some may admire our righteousness and offer submission—it cannot be ruled out.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear how generously Taizong treats surrendered generals, some may be moved to submit—it cannot be ruled out.

sentences.zh: 今明災異迭見，流寇方熾，乘時應運，定鼎中原，機不可失。」

translations.literal: Now Ming's portents and omens appear one after another, and roving bandits flourish; seizing the time and matching Heaven's mandate to fix the empire in the Central Plain—the opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Ming's omens now appear in succession and roving rebels flourish; to seize the moment, answer Heaven's mandate, and fix the empire in the Central Plain—the chance must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上深嘉之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the sovereign deeply praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, Taizong praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 九月，師圍松山，敵夜犯廷柱營，廷柱力禦，斬十餘級，獲刀甲、槍砲無算，進二等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army besieged Songshan; the enemy raided Tingzhu's camp by night; Tingzhu resisted fiercely, beheaded more than ten, captured countless blades, armor, guns, and cannon, and was promoted to second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army besieged Songshan; the enemy struck Tingzhu's camp by night, but Tingzhu beat them off, killed more than ten, and took countless arms and cannon; he was raised to second-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 七年，定漢軍八旗，置八固山，以廷柱為鑲紅旗固山額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Han Eight Banners were fixed, eight gushan established, and Tingzhu was made Gushan Ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Han Eight Banners were established with eight gushan, and Tingzhu was appointed Gushan Ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，從師入關，破李自成。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he followed the army through the pass and defeated Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he entered the pass with the army and defeated Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 五月，與固山額真巴顏等平昌平土寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, together with Gushan Ejen Bayan and others, he pacified bandits in Changping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he joined Gushan Ejen Bayan and others in suppressing bandits at Changping.

sentences.zh: 六月，與固山額真巴哈納帥師撫定山東諸郡縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, together with Gushan Ejen Bahana he led troops to pacify the prefectures and counties of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he and Gushan Ejen Bahana led troops to pacify the prefectures and counties of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七月，移師會固山額真葉臣共克太原。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he moved his army to join Gushan Ejen Yechen in jointly taking Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he marched to join Gushan Ejen Yechen in capturing Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 山西、河南悉平。

translations.literal: Shanxi and Henan were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Henan were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜白金五百兩，進一等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted five hundred taels of white silver and promoted to first-rank Angbang Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from campaign he received five hundred taels of silver and was raised to first-rank Angbang Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 四年，改一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his title was changed to first-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his title was converted to first-rank Jingqi Niha Fan.

sentences.zh: 六年，從討叛將薑瓖，复渾源、太谷、朔州、汾州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against the rebel general Jiang Xiang and recovered Hunyuan, Taigu, Shuozhou, and Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against the rebel Jiang Xiang and recovered Hunyuan, Taigu, Shuozhou, and Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，授鎮海將軍，駐防京口。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year he was appointed General Who Guards the Sea and garrisoned Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twelfth year he was made General Who Guards the Sea and posted at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 十四年二月，以老乞休，加少保兼太子太保，致仕，進三等伯，世襲。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year, citing age he requested retirement; he was given the additional ranks of Junior Guardian and Junior Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, retired from office, was promoted to third-rank Baron, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourteenth year he asked to retire on account of age; he was given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, left office, and was raised to third-rank Baron, inheritable.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，卒，贈少傅兼太子太傅，諡忠勇，立碑紀績。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year he died; he was posthumously given Junior Mentor and Junior Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was given the posthumous name Zhongyong, and a stele was erected to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighteenth year he died; he was posthumously made Junior Mentor and Junior Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongyong, and honored with a stele recording his deeds.

sentences.zh: 廷柱兄國柱，亦自廣寧降，與天柱先後授三等副將。

translations.literal: Tingzhu's elder brother Guozhu also surrendered from Guangning; he and Tianzhu were successively granted third-rank deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu's elder brother Guozhu also surrendered at Guangning; he and Tianzhu were in turn made third-rank deputy generals.

sentences.zh: 廷柱六子，三子華善，四子石琳，自有傳。

translations.literal: Tingzhu had six sons; his third son Huashan and fourth son Shilin have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhu had six sons; his third son Huashan and fourth son Shilin have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 馬光遠，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Ma Guangyuan was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guangyuan was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 明建昌參將。

translations.literal: He had been a garrison commander at Jianchang under Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming he had served as garrison commander at Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，我師克永平，光遠以所部降，命隸正藍旗，授梅勒額真，賜冠服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong, when our army took Yongping, Guangyuan surrendered with his command; he was ordered to the Plain Blue Banner, made Meile Ejen, and granted court dress, saddle, and horse.
